units.claim_summary: The discourse presents Ganesha as the deity invoked first so that an undertaking may proceed without obstruction and reach completion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காரிய நிறைவு கரிமுகனாலேயே?

units.claim_summary: A good mind is likened to a flower, and Ganesha is praised as supremely benevolent because even fierce dispositions are said to become calm before him.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மலரும் மனமும்?

units.claim_summary: The Airavatesvara-Ganesha traditions are used to portray Ganesha as one whose presence pacifies anger and protects worship from impediments.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆனைக்கா ஆனைமுகன்?

units.claim_summary: The title Vagisa is traced through religious and literary usage, with the discussion connecting mastery of speech and learning to devotional invocation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வாகீசர் யார் ??

units.claim_summary: Even when a work is dedicated to another deity, Ganesha is invoked first because the tradition assigns him the role of removing obstacles that could hinder the worship itself.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேவதையரின் இடையூறும் தீர்ப்பவர்?

units.claim_summary: A verse by the revered Mannargudi scholar is introduced as a learned but playful argument for Ganesha's primacy at the beginning of worship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மன்னார்குடிப் பெரியவாள்?

units.claim_summary: Nyayendu Sekhara is presented as a work joining Advaita Vedanta and logic, and its opening verse becomes the basis for the ensuing Ganesha argument.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “ந்யாயேந்து சேகரம்”?

units.claim_summary: The discourse explains how formal rules of Nyaya can be used inside a devotional verse and prepares the logical structure by which Ganesha's priority is defended.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிள்ளையாரும் தர்க்க சாஸ்திரமும்?

units.claim_summary: The opening Ganesha verse says that even worshippers devoted to other deities first honor Ganesha's feet so that their intended worship may proceed without impediment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “பெரியவா”ளின் பிள்ளையார் ச்லோகம்?

units.claim_summary: The tat-hetu maxim is explained as reasoning from the cause of a result, and the chapter applies that logical form to Ganesha's role in enabling other acts of worship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘தத்-ஹேது ‘ நியாயம்?

units.claim_summary: Worshippers may seek different deities for different ends, yet the chapter says they commonly invoke Ganesha first because obstacle-removal is prerequisite to those separate rites.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இதர தெய்வ உபாஸகரும் வழிபடுவது?

units.claim_summary: The word dvandva is explained through meanings of pairing, relationship, and opposition in order to clarify the expression describing Ganesha's two lotus feet.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “தொந்தம்”?

units.claim_summary: The lotus-foot image is interpreted through the lotus arising clean from mud, using the image to express purity associated with the deity's feet.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாத தாமரை?

units.claim_summary: Those who recognize that successful worship depends on freedom from impediments are portrayed as understanding the special significance of worshipping Ganesha's feet first.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “பாத பூஜைக்கார” ரின் பெருமை?

units.claim_summary: The chapter contrasts ordinary worshippers, who invoke Ganesha before turning to another deity, with a logician who treats Ganesha himself as the single supreme cause behind the desired result.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘ந்யாயம்’ அறியாதவரும் அறிந்தவரும் பண்ணுபவை?

units.claim_summary: Even if deities are conventionally associated with different benefits, the chapter argues that the supreme indwelling reality can confer any benefit through a particular deity, including Ganesha.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எல்லாப் பலன்களும் அளிக்காதவராயினும்…?

units.claim_summary: Plural forms of worship are defended as fitting ordinary human diversity in taste and temperament, while exclusive devotion is acknowledged as a rarer spiritual disposition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பல தெய்வங்கள் ஏன்??

units.claim_summary: Ganesha's obstacle-removing function is treated not as a narrow limitation but as a route through which the supreme power behind all deities may grant a wider range of benefits.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எல்லாப் பலனும் அளிக்காதவராயினும்தான்!?

units.claim_summary: The logical sufficiency of worshipping Ganesha alone is explicitly not made a rule to discard other deities; varied worship is retained as natural and legitimate for most people.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘வெரைட்டி’ வழிபாடே மனித இயற்கை?

units.claim_summary: The closing expression is interpreted as calling Ganesha uniquely capable of bestowing both worldly benefits and spiritual welfare.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இக – பர பலன்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The epithet 'two-mothered' is explained through Ganesha's mythic maternal relationships and related iconographic and textual traditions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இரண்டு தாயார்க்காரர்!?

units.claim_summary: Muruga's epithet 'six-mothered' is explained as referring to the six Krittika mothers rather than to Parvati or Ganga.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆறு தாயார்க்காரர் !?

units.claim_summary: Competing stories about Ayyappa's maternal identity are examined without forcing them into a single genealogy, and the chapter distinguishes later popular narratives from older divine-parentage motifs.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஐயப்பனின் தாயாரைப் பற்றிய பிரச்னை!?

units.claim_summary: The verse's final prayer asks Ganesha to protect the devotees, while the discourse cautions that ordinary practice still appropriately addresses different deities for their distinctive functions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விக்நேச்வரர் ரக்ஷிக்கட்டும் !?

units.claim_summary: Reasoned criticism is said to be compatible with religious scholarship only when conducted with intellectual fairness and respect rather than contempt for opponents.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்டனத்திலும் கண்ணியம்?

units.claim_summary: The story of Ganesha and the moon is used to explain a ritual prohibition and its mitigation, presenting the myth as the traditional rationale for the observance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிறையுடன் விளையாடிய பிள்ளையார்?

units.claim_summary: Examples of citra-kavya illustrate how poetic ingenuity can encode multiple meanings or visual patterns, and the discussion links such literary skill to devotional composition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சித்ர கவிதை?

units.claim_summary: A mangala verse is treated not merely as ornament but as an auspicious opening intended to orient a work toward divine grace and successful completion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “மங்கள” ச்லோகம்?

units.claim_summary: The imagery of estrangement and reunion is interpreted spiritually: apparent separation can intensify longing and culminate in a deeper union with the divine.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஊடல் – கூடலின் தத்வார்த்தம்?

units.claim_summary: A mythic episode of divine play is read as showing how apparent rivalry or conflict can conceal affection, grace, and a theological purpose beneath the surface narrative.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விளையாட்டில் மறைந்த விரோதம்?

units.claim_summary: A second verse is used as internal evidence for the interpretation of the preceding verse, showing how one poetic passage can clarify the intended sense of another.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “அந்த” ச்லோகத்திற்கு “இந்த” ச்லோகத்தின் அத்தாட்சி?

units.claim_summary: The word kalabha and related poetic usage are examined to clarify an image in the verse rather than to build a separate doctrinal claim.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about களபம்?

units.claim_summary: The prayer asks that spiritual burdens and obstacles be made light through grace, connecting the verse's wording to the devotee's dependence on divine help.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about லேசாக்கி அருள்வாராக!?

units.claim_summary: Worldly possessions are contrasted with the spiritual wealth transmitted by a guru, which is presented as a durable possession that cannot be exhausted in the same way as material property.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிற சொத்துக்களும், குரு தரும் சொத்தும்?

units.claim_summary: Devotion to God and devotion to the guru are treated as mutually reinforcing because the guru leads the disciple toward the divine and divine grace operates through the guru.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தெய்வ பக்தியும் குரு பக்தியும்?

units.claim_summary: Scriptural learning reaches fulfillment only as lived realization; the chapter distinguishes conceptual knowledge from the direct experiential knowledge expected of a true teacher.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அநுபவ ஞானம்?

units.claim_summary: The conventional contrast between brain and heart is used as a spiritual-psychological metaphor for discursive intellect and inward realization, not as a modern physiological claim.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மூளையும் இதயமும்?

units.claim_summary: Sruti, reasoning, and experience are presented as complementary: scripture supplies authority, reasoning removes misunderstanding, and realization confirms the teaching inwardly.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ச்ருதி-யுக்தி-அநுபவம்?

units.claim_summary: Devotion to God and devotion to the guru are not ultimately two rival loyalties, because the discourse locates both in a single divine source.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இரண்டு பக்திகளா??

units.claim_summary: Although worship may be directed through many forms, the ultimate giver of the fruit of worship is said to be Ishvara rather than the finite agency of the worshipper.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பலனளிப்பவன் ஈச்வரனே !?

units.claim_summary: The grace attributed to God and the grace attributed to the guru are treated as one grace operating through different relational forms.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இரண்டு க்ருபைகளா ??

units.claim_summary: Worship offered to different divine forms is said ultimately to reach the one supreme reality, so plurality of forms need not imply plurality at the highest level.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எல்லா வணக்கமும் போய்ச் சேருவது ஒருவனையே!?

units.claim_summary: Because guru and God are understood as expressions of one divine reality, the chapter argues that devotion and grace are likewise one at their deepest level.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஒரே பக்திதான்; க்ருபையும் ஒன்றுதான்!?

units.claim_summary: A change in construing the verse alters its theological emphasis, and the chapter uses grammatical interpretation to refine rather than merely repeat the preceding claim.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ச்லோகப் பொருளில் மாறுதல்?

units.claim_summary: If exclusive dependence on one figure is required, the chapter asks whether that figure should be God or guru and prepares the case for understanding their relationship rather than choosing by rivalry.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஒருவரே போதுமெனில் அவர் ஈச்வரனா, குருவா ??

units.claim_summary: Variation in religious forms is defended as matching variation in human taste; difference in outward worship can therefore coexist with a common spiritual aim.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாறுபாட்டில் ருசியே மனித இயற்கை?

units.claim_summary: Exclusive devotion is presented as an ideal of undivided concentration rather than a practical demand that every person abandon all other devotional forms.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அநன்ய பக்தி : ஆதர்சத்துக்கான யுக்தியே?

units.claim_summary: The chapter acknowledges the practical difficulty of exclusive devotion and therefore allows graded devotional practice suited to ordinary human attachments and capacities.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அநன்ய பக்தி : நடைமுறை சிரமங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Saying 'God is the guru' and 'the guru is God' are presented as complementary perspectives on divine guidance rather than as competing claims.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘ஈசனே குரு’ என்பதும், ‘குருவே ஈசன்’ என்பதும்?

units.claim_summary: The guru can be worshipped as God because the discourse treats divine wisdom and grace as becoming accessible to the disciple through the teacher's person.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருவையே ஈசனாகக் கொள்வதெப்படி??

units.claim_summary: Guru worship is distinguished by immediacy: the disciple can receive instruction, correction, and compassionate guidance from a living relational form of the sacred.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு வழிபாட்டின் சிறப்பம்சங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The Yathoktakari story is used to illustrate a deity responding to a devotee's word, emphasizing the extraordinary intimacy attributed to saint, disciple, and temple deity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about யதோக்தகாரி : சொன்ன வண்ணம் செய்த பெருமாள்?

units.claim_summary: Kanchipuram's many Divya Desams are noted as evidence of the city's dense Sri Vaishnava sacred geography and its association with multiple forms of Vishnu worship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காஞ்சியிலுள்ள “திவ்ய தேசங்கள்”?

units.claim_summary: The Vaikuntha Perumal temple is discussed in relation to Pallava patronage and the coexistence of Saiva and Vaishnava traditions, with historical claims treated as requiring external verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பல்லவரும் சைவ-வைணவமும் : வைகுண்டப் பெருமாள் கோயில்?

units.claim_summary: Several traditions about Pallava origins are surveyed and kept distinct, illustrating the uncertainty of reconstructing dynastic beginnings from later literary and historical materials.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பல்லவர் தோற்றுவாய்?

units.claim_summary: The greatness of Tiruvekka's deity is explained through the temple's Alvar tradition and the deity's reputation for responding to the saint's devotion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருவெஃகா பெருமாளின் பெருமை?

units.claim_summary: Kanikannan is portrayed as combining compassion with fearless loyalty, and his refusal to compromise becomes the narrative trigger for the saint and deity leaving Kanchi.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கணிகண்ணன் : அருள் நெஞ்சும் அஞ்சாநெஞ்சும்?

units.claim_summary: The Alvar leaves Kanchi with his disciple after the disciple is expelled, and the deity is narrated as accompanying them in response to the Alvar’s appeal.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சொன்ன வண்ணம் செய்தது !?

units.claim_summary: The king recognizes the disaster caused by the departure, seeks reconciliation, and the Alvar’s return is narrated together with the deity reversing the earlier act exactly as requested.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சொன்ன வண்ணம் செய்தது !?

units.claim_summary: The episode is explicitly interpreted to teach that trust in the guru can become the effective means through which divine grace is obtained.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சொன்ன வண்ணம் செய்தது !?

units.claim_summary: The story is used to argue that attachment to a realized guru can itself bring the divine near, because the guru's prayer or spiritual authority mediates what the disciple cannot secure alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வரனையும் வருவித்துத் தரும் குரு?

units.claim_summary: Somasi Mara Nayanar's desire that Shiva personally receive the offering at his soma sacrifice is introduced as a quest for direct divine acceptance rather than merely ritual confidence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸோமாசி மாற நாயனார்?

units.claim_summary: Sundaramurti is portrayed as possessing exceptional intimacy with Shiva, making him the intermediary through whom Somasi Mara hopes to invite the deity to the sacrifice.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்வாமியிடம் ஸ்வாதீனம் கொண்ட ஸ்வாமிகள்?

units.claim_summary: The conduct of saints and of God is said not always to fit ordinary reasoning, so apparent irregularities in hagiographic narratives should not be judged hastily by conventional expectations.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நம் அறிவை மீறிய மஹான்களின் போக்கு?

units.claim_summary: Somasi Mara's persistent service to Sundaramurti is presented as humble guru-oriented devotion through which he seeks the saint's help in obtaining Shiva's presence at the sacrifice.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தூதுபோன தூதுவளை !?

units.claim_summary: The Somasi Mara sacred-test narrative portrays Shiva arriving at the sacrifice in a socially transgressive form, with the devotee recognizing the divine presence when others reject it.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரமன் வைத்த பரீக்ஷை?

units.claim_summary: The narrative is explicitly used to argue that one who cannot reach God by personal power may rely on a realized guru, and that steadfast trust and devotion to the guru are the required response.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரமன் வைத்த பரீக்ஷை?

units.claim_summary: Even if a guru has ordinary limitations, the chapter argues that devotion need not be invalidated because the omnipresent divine can work through that teacher for the disciple's good.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருவுக்குக் குறை இருந்தாலும்…?

units.claim_summary: Guru devotion is presented as practically more immediate than devotion to an unseen deity because the guru can correct, encourage, guide, and personally reassure the disciple.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருபக்தியின் அநுகூலங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Meditation on a personally known guru is presented as easier to stabilize than visualization of an unseen deity, while the teaching ultimately identifies guru and God rather than making them competing objects of devotion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருபக்தியின் அநுகூலங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Three devotional orientations toward the guru are distinguished, ranging from seeing the teacher as guide to regarding the teacher as inseparable from God or as the devotee's sole spiritual refuge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மூன்று விதமான பாவங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: A disciple who serves the guru with wholehearted devotion is said to receive divine assistance toward knowledge and liberation even without separately calculating those results.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு பக்திக்கு ஈசன் செய்யும் அருள்?

units.claim_summary: The guru and disciple are presented as embodying reciprocal duties: the disciple offers service and trust, while the guru undertakes a disproportionately greater responsibility for the disciple's spiritual progress.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு-சிஷ்யர் : இருபெரும் தர்மங்களின் உருவகம்?

units.claim_summary: Different devotional temperaments are allowed to approach God directly or through a guru; the essential requirement is sincere adherence to a path that leads toward moral and spiritual good.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எந்த பாவத்தினாலும் ஈசனருள் பெறலாம்?

units.claim_summary: Learning from a guru is preferred to relying only on books or private experience because personal instruction is said to check intellectual pride and align knowledge with disciplined practice.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருமுகமாக அறிவதன் சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: The familiar guru verse is examined so that Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara, and Parabrahman are understood as analogies for the guru's spiritual function rather than as a simplistic identification of cosmic job-holders.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மும்மூர்த்தியரை மூலப்பொருளாக அல்லாமல்!?

units.claim_summary: Brahma's relative absence from popular festivals is introduced as a devotional-historical puzzle that the following discussion attempts to explain.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பண்டிகை இல்லாத கடவுள்?

units.claim_summary: Brahma's scarcity of independent temples is presented as a striking contrast with the abundance of shrines and festivals devoted to other major deities.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கோயிலில்லாத கடவுள்?

units.claim_summary: Shaiva narratives explaining Brahma’s lack of widespread temple worship are presented as sectarian traditions rather than as a universally accepted historical explanation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பூஜை இல்லாத காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: The discussion broadens beyond one sectarian story, comparing other theological explanations and treating Brahma’s limited popular worship as a question that cannot be settled by the Shaiva curse narrative alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பூஜை இல்லாத காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Sri Vaishnava temple practice centers Vishnu, his consort, attendants, incarnations, and devotees, and Brahma's subordinate place is explained within that sectarian theological structure.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வைஷ்ணவ ஆலய மூர்த்திகள்?

units.claim_summary: Agamic temple planning nevertheless assigns Brahma a place, reflecting his status within the Trimurti even where he is not the principal object of worship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆகமத்தில் ப்ரம்மா?

units.claim_summary: Creation itself is defended as an act within divine order rather than a cruelty attributable to Brahma, even though embodied beings may emotionally resent the creator because birth entails suffering.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரம்மாவின் தொழில் கருணையானதே!?

units.claim_summary: Rudra, Shiva, Nataraja, and Maheshvara are distinguished terminologically so that the guru verse's use of 'Maheshvara' can be interpreted in relation to Shiva's cosmic functions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ருத்ரன் – சிவன் (சிவம், நடராஜா) – மஹேச்வரன்?

units.claim_summary: From a Sri Vaishnava standpoint Vishnu is not merely the preserver within a threefold division of labor but the supreme reality of which the other divine functions are subordinate expressions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வைஷ்ணவத்தில்?

units.claim_summary: The guru verse culminates in salutation to the guru as Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara, and ultimately Parabrahman, setting up the question of what makes such salutation spiritually warranted.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரவே நம:?

units.claim_summary: The chapter asks why identification with the Trimurti or with Brahman should by itself justify salutation, forcing the argument to explain the guru's liberating function rather than rely on titles.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எதற்காக நமஸ்காரம்??

units.claim_summary: The guru is not worshipped merely because the three cosmic functions are attributed to him; the chapter argues that those functions, taken literally, do not themselves explain liberation or the devotee's reason for reverence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முத்தொழில் புரிபவர் என்பதற்காக வழிபாடில்லை?

units.claim_summary: Major deities such as Vishnu, Shiva, Devi, Lakshmi, Ganesha, Muruga, and Hanuman are treated devotionally as manifestations of complete divine power, while Brahma is discussed differently in popular worship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முழுமுதலாக விளங்கும் மூர்த்திகள்?

units.claim_summary: Brahma's limited worship is explained through devotional psychology: creation alone does not make him the devotee's chosen refuge, and inherited practice supplies few relational forms through which personal attachment to him develops.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரம்மாவுக்கு மட்டும் ஏன் விலக்கு ??

units.claim_summary: The Trimurti scheme is explained as a theological way of distributing creation, preservation, and dissolution within a larger divine unity that includes Brahma without making any one finite function the whole supreme reality.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரம்மாவை உள்ளடக்கி த்ரிமூர்த்தியர் ஏற்பட்ட காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Saraswati's lack of many independent temples is explained through a traditional marital ideal linking her public cultic prominence to Brahma's, a gendered norm that requires historical context rather than endorsement.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸரஸ்வதிக்கு ஆலயம் இல்லாததேன்??

units.claim_summary: Brahma is described in the tradition as associated with Saraswati, Gayatri, and Savitri, introducing the differing roles assigned to these consorts.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸாவித்ரி, காயத்ரி, நாரதர் விஷயம்?

units.claim_summary: Narada’s lack of a fixed temple cult is linked to traditions of perpetual wandering, Daksha’s curse, and his place in a devotional guru lineage centered on divine-name repetition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸாவித்ரி, காயத்ரி, நாரதர் விஷயம்?

units.claim_summary: Brahma is located within transmitted guru lineages as recipient of teaching from Narayana and teacher of Vasishtha, while differing sectarian lineage schemes are acknowledged rather than harmonized.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு பரம்பரையில் ப்ரம்மா?

units.claim_summary: Neither the Trimurti analogy nor nirguna Brahman alone explains salutation: the chapter argues that reverence becomes meaningful only through the guru's relation to the bound disciple.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நமஸ்கரிப்பதற்குக் காரணமில்லை !?

units.claim_summary: The guru's 'creation, preservation, and destruction' are reinterpreted spiritually as awakening knowledge, sustaining the disciple's growth, and destroying ignorance, which is the basis for the Trimurti analogy.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வித்யாஸமான முத்தொழில்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Unlike cosmic processes that continue embodied existence, the guru's analogous three functions are praised because they are directed toward freedom from karma and samsara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நமஸ்காரத்திற்கு உரியவராக?

units.claim_summary: The guru is called Parabrahman because realization of Brahman is presented not merely as information the teacher possesses but as the teacher's deepest spiritual identity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரப் பிரம்மமாக?

units.claim_summary: A true guru is defined as one who has crossed the ocean of samsara and is therefore capable of guiding another person across it rather than merely describing the destination.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கரை ஏறியவர், ஏற்றுவிப்பவர்?

units.claim_summary: Texts attributed to Shankara are used to characterize the teacher as scripturally grounded, realized, compassionate, desireless, and capable of adapting instruction to the disciple's needs.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசார்யாள் அளிக்கும் ஆசார்ய லக்ஷணம்?

units.claim_summary: Even when identified with Brahman, the guru remains an object of salutation because compassion is said to take relational form for the sake of correcting and uplifting disciples.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரம்மமாயினும் நமஸ்காரத்துக்குரியவரே!?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's prayer is interpreted as treating the very act and disposition of saluting the guru as a form of spiritual wealth worth possessing continuously.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நமஸ்காரமே செல்வம்: ஆசார்யாள் உணர்த்துவது?

units.claim_summary: The words Amba and Mata are examined as forms of 'mother,' preparing the interpretation of Lakshmi as a maternal divine figure addressed in the verse.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அம்பா, மாதா: அம்மன், தாயார்?

units.claim_summary: Salutation to Lakshmi is said to yield worldly prosperity and royal fortune while the verse is also interpreted as moving beyond such goods toward purification from sin and spiritual welfare.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நமஸ்காரம் அளிக்கும் பயன்கள்?

units.claim_summary: A philological correction prefers the sense of 'uprooting' deeply rooted wrongdoing over merely 'removing' it, and the chapter uses that distinction to sharpen the prayer's spiritual meaning.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஒரு திருத்தம்: ‘துரித உத்தரணம்’?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's prayer for removal of sin is read as an intercession for devotees rather than a confession of personal impurity by the teacher himself.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மறுமைப் பயன் கோரி?

units.claim_summary: The placement of the emphatic particle eva is examined grammatically, and the preferred reading makes unwavering salutation itself the devotee's secure possession rather than a selfish exclusive claim.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “ஏவ” எதில் சேர வேண்டும்??

units.claim_summary: Vishnu is invoked as teacher of the three worlds, and Lakshmi's salutation is interpreted as inseparable from that divine teaching relationship and its power to uproot wrongdoing.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மூவுலக குரு?

units.claim_summary: A traditional maxim contrasts contempt for the guru with poison and sound teaching received from the guru with nectar, emphasizing the spiritual consequences assigned to reverence and receptivity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு வந்தனை – நிந்தனை: அம்ருதம் – விஷம்?

units.claim_summary: The guru's 'effort' is interpreted as the active work of lifting the disciple out of bondage, so the devotee prays to retain guru-salutation as the means that makes such rescue possible.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருவின் ‘முயற்சி’ உத்தரணத்தைக் குறிப்பதே?

units.claim_summary: Pravritti and nivritti are contrasted as paths oriented respectively toward ordered worldly engagement and toward final release, with lasting freedom ranked above transient results.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரவ்ருத்தி – நிவ்ருத்தி?

units.claim_summary: Two broad spiritual paths are presented for different human capacities: disciplined engagement through prescribed action and withdrawal oriented toward direct realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இருவித மக்களுக்கான இரு வழிகள்?

units.claim_summary: The karma path is said to yield either desired worldly or heavenly results when pursued for fruits, or purification of mind when duty is performed without attachment, the latter becoming karma-yoga that prepares for knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கர்ம மார்க்கத்தின் இருவித பலன்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The discourse narrates a historical decline in which desire for ritual fruits displaced the renunciatory aim of karma-yoga and associates that development with a polemical account of Purva Mimamsa.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காலப் போக்கில் கர்ம யோக நலிவு?

units.claim_summary: Divine and scriptural teachers are said to transmit both the path of action and the path of renunciation, with the Bhagavad Gita presented as integrating disciplined action, devotion, and knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இரு மார்க்கங்களின் உபதேசங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Bhakti is presented as a path that turns emotional attachment toward God, concentrates the mind, and can support the transition from action to higher realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பக்தி?

units.claim_summary: The Gita's several yogas are treated as complementary disciplines suited to different stages rather than as unrelated competing systems.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கீதை கூறும் யோகங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Advaita is called the enduring yoga because its goal is the non-dual realization that remains when action, devotional duality, and other provisional disciplines have fulfilled their preparatory roles.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘நிரந்தர’ யோகமான அத்வைதம்?

units.claim_summary: Krishna's teaching is portrayed as a restoration of an ancient yoga that had declined, reconnecting worldly duty with disciplined action, devotion, and liberating knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்ணன் செய்த புனருத்தாரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Krishna and Shankara are linked as restorers who reassert a path from disciplined action and devotion toward knowledge when religious practice is said to have lost that orientation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்ணனும் சங்கரரும்?

units.claim_summary: Earlier divine incarnations are recalled as precedents for intervention when dharma requires restoration, preparing the argument for Shankara's appearance as an avatara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பூர்வகால அவதாரங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The chapter presents a traditional Kali-yuga chronology and places Shankara within it, a historical dating claim that is kept as attributed tradition rather than independently established chronology.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கலியுகம் : தொடக்க காலத்திலும் பிற்காலத்திலும்?

units.claim_summary: Kali's danger is described as the ability of harmful tendencies to appear under attractive moral or religious forms, so discernment is presented as necessary even when a teaching seems benevolent.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கலியின் பேரபாயம் : மயக்கு வேஷம்?

units.claim_summary: Founders of newer religions are acknowledged as capable of moral seriousness, yet the discourse classifies their systems according to whether they accept the Veda and treats departures from Vedic authority polemically.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about புது மத ஸ்தாபகர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Buddhism and Jainism are compared with Hindu traditions on nonviolence, social order, and religious discipline; the resulting claims are represented as the discourse's interreligious and social argument rather than as neutral history.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பௌத்த சமண மதங்களும் ஹிந்து மதமும்?

units.claim_summary: The chapter defends Vedic animal sacrifice within its own scriptural rationale while condemning excessive killing, and it uses the Pracinabarhis-Narada story to warn that ritual violence can still incur moral consequences.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about யாகத்தில் ஹிம்ஸை?

units.claim_summary: The discourse says other religions should not be attacked out of hostility, but it also argues that one's own tradition may be defended by reasoned criticism; disagreement should target doctrines without hatred toward persons.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிறமத கண்டனத்திற்காக அல்ல: ஸ்வயமத கண்டனம் கூடாது என்றே!?

units.claim_summary: The portrayal of Kali as deliberately leading people away from Vedic religion is treated as a theological explanation of religious plurality, while the chapter wrestles with whether morally serious teachers can simply be reduced to malicious agents.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கலி அதமர்த்திற்கே ஸங்கற்பிக்கப்பட்டதா??

units.claim_summary: Shankara's 'victory' is framed primarily as the successful re-establishment of a religious and philosophical order through teaching and debate rather than as physical conquest.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சங்கர ‘விஜயம்’?

units.claim_summary: The traditional claim that Shankara encountered and answered seventy-two schools is used to emphasize the plurality of positions in his period and the breadth attributed to his intellectual mission.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எழுபத்திரண்டு மதங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's achievement is presented as extraordinary because a young renunciant is said to have travelled widely, debated many schools, produced major works, and reorganized religious practice without political force.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசார்யாளின் ஆச்சரிய ஸாதனை?

units.claim_summary: The chapter argues that Shankara's own position should be understood as inclusive Vedic religion rather than merely one sect among many, because it claims to accommodate diverse Vedic practices within a graded framework.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அனைத்தும் அடங்கிய வைதிகம் ஆசார்யாள் மதமே?

units.claim_summary: Other religions and schools are evaluated according to how much of Vedic revelation and practice they accept, while the discourse insists that criticism should distinguish partial truth from what it regards as incomplete or non-Vedic conclusions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இதர மதங்களைப் பற்றி?

units.claim_summary: Belief in a governing deity is treated as an important dividing line among Indian philosophical systems, with the chapter distinguishing theistic, non-theistic, and differently theistic positions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கடவுட்கொள்கை?

units.claim_summary: Buddhist and Jain systems are discussed in relation to ordinary religious psychology, with the argument that highly austere doctrines may fit exceptional ascetics better than the devotional and ritual needs of the general population.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பௌத்த-ஜைனமும் பொது ஜனங்களின் மனப்போக்கும்?

units.claim_summary: Lokayata is presented as an openly materialist position that rejects afterlife, Vedic authority, and spiritual liberation, making it the clearest contrast in the discourse's classification of schools.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அப்பட்டமான லோகாயதம்?

units.claim_summary: Some systems are said to accept portions of the Veda while rejecting Vedanta's final teaching; the chapter distinguishes formal Vedic affiliation from acceptance of the Upanishadic conclusion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேதத்தை ஒப்பியும் வேதாந்தத்தை ஒப்பாத மதங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: A system is called fully Vedic only when it accepts the Veda as a whole, including both ritual obligations and the culminating Vedantic teaching, rather than selecting one portion against another.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முழுதும் வேத ஸம்மதமானாலே வைதிகம்?

units.claim_summary: Religious movements that overturn inherited Vedic structures are characterized as revolutionary, a polemical category used to contrast reform from within with rejection of the scriptural framework.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about புரட்சி மதங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: An avatara is said to become necessary when ordinary teachers and institutions can no longer reverse a severe decline of dharma.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதாரம் தோன்ற அவசியச் சூழ்நிலை?

units.claim_summary: The doctrine of avatara is explained as the supreme reality freely assuming an embodied form without becoming bound like an ordinary being, in order to restore dharma and guide people through a visible human example.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதார தத்வம்?

units.claim_summary: Scriptural statements about divine birth are read as hints that an avatara appears through divine freedom and control of maya rather than through ordinary karmic compulsion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதார ரஹஸ்ய சூசனை?

units.claim_summary: Mere divine intention is said to be insufficient for the pedagogical purpose of an avatara because people need an embodied model whose conduct can be observed and imitated in concrete moral situations.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஏன் ஸங்கல்ப மாத்திரத்தால் கூடாது??

units.claim_summary: An avatara combines recognizable human limitations and emotions with a divine dimension, allowing people to identify with the figure while still receiving an extraordinary model of dharmic action.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதாரத்தில் மனிதத்தன்மையும் தெய்வத்தன்மையும்?

units.claim_summary: Beyond restoring dharma, incarnation is presented as divine desire for intimate relationship with creatures; human form makes mutual affection and ordinary companionship possible without abolishing transcendent divinity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கலந்து பழகும் ஆசைக்காகவும்?

units.claim_summary: The apparent humanity of an avatara should not, according to the discourse, be taken as evidence of bondage to maya, because the incarnation is said to remain inwardly free while voluntarily assuming human conditions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதாரம் குறித்து ஐயம் கூடாது?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's appearance is placed against a narrative of unprecedented religious disorder in which competing systems, ritual decline, and confusion about Vedic teaching are said to have reached a crisis.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முன்னெப்போதுமில்லா தர்மக் குலைவு?

units.claim_summary: The promise in the Gita that the divine appears when dharma declines is applied to Shankara, while the chapter addresses the problem of calling a historical teacher an avatara without collapsing him into Krishna's specific form.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கீதா வாக்ய பரிபாலனம்: பிரச்னையும் தீர்வும்?

units.claim_summary: Renunciation is presented as the fitting form of Shankara's mission because a sannyasin can travel, teach beyond household ties, model detachment, and speak across regional and social boundaries.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஏன் ஸந்நியாஸியாக அவதாரம்??

units.claim_summary: The chapter explains why Shankara's renunciatory disposition is portrayed as evident already in brahmacharya, making later sannyasa a culmination rather than an abrupt rejection of an earlier life orientation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரம்மசர்ய ஆச்ரமத்திலும்?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's birth in a Brahmin family is explained within the discourse's traditional varna framework as fitting a mission centered on Vedic learning and teaching, a normative caste claim requiring historical context.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அந்தண குல அவதாரம்?

units.claim_summary: Shiva and Vishnu are presented as distinct divine roles assumed by one ultimate reality, so sectarian opposition between them is rejected even while their conventional functions are distinguished.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விஷ்ணு அவதாரமும் சிவாவதாரமும்: சிவ-விஷ்ணு ஒற்றுமை வேற்றுமைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Krishna’s Gita revelation is used to show that Vishnu’s avatar can manifest functions conventionally associated with Shiva, including destruction and liberation, without dissolving the shared divine identity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விஷ்ணு அவதாரமும் சிவாவதாரமும்: சிவ-விஷ்ணு ஒற்றுமை வேற்றுமைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Earlier avatars are contrasted with Krishna in terms of the social and historical role assigned to each, with Krishna portrayed as combining royal protection of dharma with explicit spiritual instruction.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விஷ்ணு அவதாரமும் சிவாவதாரமும்: சிவ-விஷ்ணு ஒற்றுமை வேற்றுமைகள்?

units.claim_summary: For the Kali-age crisis described here, Shankara is presented as a Shiva avatar whose principal mission is knowledge-teaching rather than political or martial destruction.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விஷ்ணு அவதாரமும் சிவாவதாரமும்: சிவ-விஷ்ணு ஒற்றுமை வேற்றுமைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Gita passages that both distinguish and identify Krishna with Ishvara are used to argue that surrender to the Lord and recognition of the indwelling Self converge rather than contradict one another.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விஷ்ணு அவதாரமும் சிவாவதாரமும்: சிவ-விஷ்ணு ஒற்றுமை வேற்றுமைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Shiva, characterized as the deity of knowledge and renunciation, is presented as especially fitting for an incarnation whose principal mission is the restoration of liberating knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஞான சிவனே ஞானவதாரமாவது?

units.claim_summary: Dakshinamurti is treated as Shiva together with inseparable Shakti, so Shankara's identification with that form includes both transcendent knowledge and the power needed for active teaching in the world.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சக்தி உள்ளடங்கிய தக்ஷிணாமூர்த்தியின் அவதாரம்?

units.claim_summary: Shankara is presented as belonging simultaneously to Shakta, Saiva, and Vaishnava devotional worlds, with sectarian forms treated as compatible expressions within his broader Smarta-Advaita synthesis.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாக்தர், சைவர், வைஷ்ணவர் மூன்றுமான ஆசார்யாள்?

units.claim_summary: The divine teacher is characterized as auspicious not merely by name but by the capacity to transform ignorance into knowledge and religious division into a path toward higher unity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மங்கள மயமான தெய்வகுரு?

units.claim_summary: The circumstances preceding Shankara's birth are narrated as a sacred prelude in which parental devotion and divine intention prepare the ground for the avatara story.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதாரத்திற்குப் பூர்வாங்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The apparently actionless absolute is nevertheless described as compassionate, and incarnation is explained as the paradoxical expression of that compassion without compromising ultimate non-action.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about செயலற்றவரின் கருணையுள்ளம்?

units.claim_summary: Advaita is said to become evident when the mind that sustains subject-object duality subsides, leaving non-dual awareness rather than a second object to be known.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனமென்ற த்வைதம் மறைவதே அத்வைதம்?

units.claim_summary: The non-dual culmination is explicitly distinguished from nihilistic emptiness and described instead as fullness of being, consciousness, and bliss.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சூன்யமில்லை; ஸச்சிதானந்த பூர்ணமே !?

units.claim_summary: At the highest level the distinction between individual self and supreme self is denied, with bondage attributed to ignorance of their underlying identity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜீவாத்ம-பரமாத்ம பேதமும் இல்லை?

units.claim_summary: Ishvara can operate with maya and still be called a knower because, unlike the individual being, the divine is said to possess and govern maya rather than be deluded by it.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாயா ஸஹிதனாயினும் ஈசன் ஞானியே!?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's avatara mission is presented as leading people through disciplined action and devotion toward knowledge, not as demanding immediate non-dual realization from persons unprepared for it.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதார நோக்கம்: கர்மா-பக்தி வழியே ஞானம் அடைவித்தல்?

units.claim_summary: In ordinary action no benefit is entirely free of side effects, so moral discernment must weigh mixed consequences rather than imagine that every helpful act is unqualified good.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கலப்படமற்ற நன்மை எதுவுமில்லை?

units.claim_summary: Even service intended to help others can produce dependency, pride, unintended harm, or new entanglements; the chapter therefore subordinates social action to self-discipline and freedom from egoistic doership.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உபகாரப் பணியிலும் அபகாரம்!?

units.claim_summary: The paradoxical purpose of the avatara is said to be teaching people ultimately to transcend compulsive action and rest in the non-acting self, even though the teacher is outwardly extraordinarily active.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எதுவும் செய்யாமலிருப்பதற்கான அவதாரம்!?

units.claim_summary: Good action remains necessary in practical life because it purifies character and mind, even when the final Advaitic goal is described as freedom from identification with action.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நடைமுறையில் நற்கர்மத்தின் பயன்?

units.claim_summary: Actions are prescribed as a means of eventually outgrowing attachment to action: disciplined performance is a preparatory path toward effortless non-doership.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about செயலற்றுப் போக வழியாகவே செயல்களும்!?

units.claim_summary: The practical instruction is to perform one's necessary work, while keeping non-attachment and inner stillness as the ultimate spiritual aim.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நடைமுறை: காரியம் செய்வது; லக்ஷ்யம்: சும்மாயிருப்பது?

units.claim_summary: Even good deeds can preserve bondage when the agent's pride in being the doer remains; limitations and mixed results are therefore used to weaken egoistic ownership of action.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கர்த்தாவின் அஹம்பாவம் நீங்கவே நல்லதிலும் கெடுதல்?

units.claim_summary: Service is not rejected as selfish merely because the practitioner gains purification from it; benefit to oneself and benefit to others can coexist when personal reward is not the controlling motive.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்வயநலமாகாது?

units.claim_summary: A realized person's inward stillness is itself said to benefit the world through presence and example, so visible activity is not made the sole measure of service.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சும்மாயிருப்பதாலும் லோகோபகாரம்?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's intense activity is interpreted as a teaching device whose deeper message is freedom from compulsive action and identification with doership.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காரியமின்மையைச் சொல்லவே ஓயாக்காரிய அவதாரம்?

units.claim_summary: The name Shankara is analyzed through its components and sacred associations to present the teacher as one who brings auspiciousness, linking etymology, Shiva theology, and the mission attributed to the avatara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சம்-பு சம்-கரரானார்?

units.claim_summary: The discourse assembles early-scriptural and later exegetical material, including a Rig-Vedic locus as interpreted through Vishnudharmottara, as evidence used within tradition for Shankara’s divine-avatar status.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வராவதார ப்ரமாணங்கள்: வேத-இதிஹாச-புராணங்களில்?

units.claim_summary: Names and ascetic imagery in Sri Rudram are interpreted as foreshadowing the Sambhu-to-Shankara relationship and the form of a shaven renunciant teacher.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வராவதார ப்ரமாணங்கள்: வேத-இதிஹாச-புராணங்களில்?

units.claim_summary: Itihasa-Purana and sectarian source traditions are cited as narrating Shiva’s descent as Shankara for restoration of Vedic teaching; these remain source-attributed historical-theological claims.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வராவதார ப்ரமாணங்கள்: வேத-இதிஹாச-புராணங்களில்?

units.claim_summary: Additional Purana traditions and later source testimonies are surveyed as a cumulative textual case for Shankara’s avatar status, without treating the number of sources as proof of historical independence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வராவதார ப்ரமாணங்கள்: வேத-இதிஹாச-புராணங்களில்?

units.claim_summary: Suresvara’s descriptions of Shankara are read as testimony from a direct disciple that identifies the teacher with Shiva while praising his spiritual authority.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நேர் சிஷ்யர்கள் தரும் சான்று?

units.claim_summary: Totaka’s devotional praise is used as a second direct-disciple witness to Shankara’s exceptional spiritual and divine status.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நேர் சிஷ்யர்கள் தரும் சான்று?

units.claim_summary: Padmapada’s praise develops extended Shiva-Shankara parallels and is treated as another disciple-level witness within the hagiographic tradition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நேர் சிஷ்யர்கள் தரும் சான்று?

units.claim_summary: Passages attributed to Shankara himself are examined for indications of his self-understanding and mission, while the discourse avoids simply equating devotional self-reference with independent historical verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவரே அளிக்கும் சான்று?

units.claim_summary: The pre-Shankara teacher lineage is reconstructed from traditional guru lists, and differences among lineage accounts are treated as evidence to be preserved rather than silently harmonized.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பூர்வாசார்ய பரம்பரை?

units.claim_summary: The lineage from Vasishtha through Vyasa is narrated as a succession of authoritative teachers transmitting Vedic and Vedantic knowledge across generations.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வஸிஷ்டரிலிருந்து வ்யாஸர் வரை?

units.claim_summary: Suka is portrayed as an archetype of innate realization and renunciation, and stories about his relation to Vyasa are used to explain how realization and formal instruction can coexist.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சுக ப்ரஹ்மம்?

units.claim_summary: The Patanjali-carita tradition is introduced as a source for stories connecting Patanjali, Gaudapada, and later Advaita lineage figures, with its narrative status kept distinct from independently verified history.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “பதஞ்ஜலி சரிதம்”?

units.claim_summary: A devotional image of Shiva's dance in Vishnu's heart is used to express theological intimacy between the two deities rather than sectarian opposition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருமாலின் இதயத்தின் சிவ நடனம்?

units.claim_summary: The ajapa or hamsa motif interprets the natural rhythm of breath as an unceasing sacred movement and contemplative reminder of the self.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அஜபா – ஹம்ஸ நடனம்?

units.claim_summary: Patanjali is presented in hagiographic tradition as an incarnation of Adisesha, linking the guru lineage to a mythic divine genealogy.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆதிசேஷன் அவதாரம்?

units.claim_summary: Patanjali is praised as serving mind, speech, and body through yoga, grammar, and medicine, presenting disciplined knowledge in all three domains as a form of purification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திரிகரணத்திற்கும் திருத்தொண்டு?

units.claim_summary: The discussion turns to the literary forms of sutra, bhashya, and vartika and to the transmission of grammar, distinguishing those scholarly genres from the preceding threefold spiritual analogy.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திரிகரணத்திற்கும் திருத்தொண்டு?

units.claim_summary: A miracle story of teaching a thousand disciples simultaneously portrays Patanjali's extraordinary pedagogical power and belongs to hagiographic rather than independently verified history.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆயிரம் சீடருக்கு அதிசயப் பாடம்!?

units.claim_summary: The Brahmarakshasa episode is introduced through traditional ideas about learned beings becoming dangerous spirits, a supernatural framework represented as hagiography rather than fact.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிரம்மரக்ஷஸ்; ராக்ஷஸ ஜாதி?

units.claim_summary: A violation of the teacher's instruction in the Patanjali narrative is said to produce disastrous consequences, underscoring obedience within the hagiographic story's moral logic.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விபரீதம் விளைந்தது!?

units.claim_summary: Gauda and Dravida are introduced as lineage and regional designations whose meanings must not automatically be equated with modern ethnic categories.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கௌடர்; திராவிடர்?

units.claim_summary: The disciple who survives the catastrophe receives both curse and blessing, turning punishment in the narrative into the mechanism by which the teaching lineage continues.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தப்பித்த சீடருக்குச் சாபமும் அநுக்ரஹமும்?

units.claim_summary: Gauda is narrated as living under a supernatural curse and testing travelers until a qualified student appears, a hagiographic frame for the transmission of grammar.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கௌடரின் பிற்கால சரித்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: Chandrasarma’s encounter with Gauda becomes an intense teacher-disciple transmission narrative in which mastery is acquired under extraordinary conditions and the teacher’s curse is released.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கௌடரின் பிற்கால சரித்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: Gauda then turns from grammatical mastery toward renunciation and realization, becoming Gaudapada and linking the lineage to Mandukya teaching and devotional practice.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கௌடரின் பிற்கால சரித்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: A realized knower is not portrayed as incapable of devotion; the chapter argues that knowledge and bhakti can coexist without contradiction when devotion is free of ignorance about ultimate reality.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஞானியும் பக்தியும்?

units.claim_summary: Later teachers and traditions praise Gaudapada's stature, and those encomia are used as lineage testimony rather than as independent proof of every biographical detail.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசார்யாளின் போற்றுதல்?

units.claim_summary: Chandrasarma’s arrival and recovery are narrated as the transition from the extraordinary grammar episode into ordinary social life.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சந்திரசர்மாவின் சரித்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: A complex marriage-and-householder narrative explains the family traditions attributed to Chandrasarma before his renunciation and later identity as Govinda Bhagavatpada.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சந்திரசர்மாவின் சரித்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: Brahma reappears in the guru lineage as an early recipient and transmitter of sacred knowledge, reinforcing the lineage argument rather than popular temple worship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு பரம்பரையில் ப்ரம்மா?

units.claim_summary: The discussion distinguishes nirvana and realized freedom from mere physical death, using Suka and other realized figures to illustrate freedom from ordinary social identification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about (நிர்வாணம்)?

units.claim_summary: The category of one beyond ordinary varna-ashrama identity is explained as describing realization rather than a new social license for an unprepared aspirant.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about (நிர்வாணம்)?

units.claim_summary: Different renunciate categories are distinguished, especially the movement from disciplined sannyasa toward the spontaneous freedom attributed to paramahamsa or avadhuta realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about (நிர்வாணம்)?

units.claim_summary: Scriptural examples are used to show that realized freedom may appear in different external life situations, so outward form alone is not made the criterion of knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about (நிர்வாணம்)?

units.claim_summary: The sannyasa name 'Shankara' is interpreted as carrying Shiva's auspicious associations and as fitting the teacher's renunciatory identity and mission.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸந்நியாஸ நாமம்: சங்கர நாம மஹிமை?

units.claim_summary: Parallels with Ramanuja are noted to show that major acharya traditions can share patterns of discipleship, institution, and devotional mission despite doctrinal differences.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ராமாநுஜர் ஒற்றுமை?

units.claim_summary: Govinda Bhagavatpada is praised as a realized guru whose teaching capacity is presented as equal to the exceptional disciple he is destined to train.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கோவிந்தரின் சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: A hagiographic lineage narrative links Govinda and the Patanjali tradition to a divine plan for Shankara’s mission and to the completion of the guru’s own earthly work.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கோவிந்தரின் சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Biographical traditions about what follows Shankara’s training are presented as variant source material rather than silently harmonized into a single chronology.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கோவிந்தரின் சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: The closing discussion interprets names and auspicious numerical associations around victory and the Adisesha lineage as devotional-hagiographic symbolism rather than independent historical proof.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கோவிந்தரின் சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: The acharya lineage is described as a succession of specially qualified teachers whose authority lies in realization and transmission rather than merely hereditary office.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அதிகார புருஷர் வரிசையே ஆசார்ய பரம்பரை?

units.claim_summary: The parental prayer for a child and the divine boon that follows are narrated as the hagiographic cause of Shankara's birth, including the traditional choice between longevity and extraordinary spiritual greatness.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேண்டுதலும் வரமும்?

units.claim_summary: The narrative assigns incarnations to several gods and celestial beings around Shankara's mission, embedding his biography in a coordinated divine-drama framework.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேவர்களின் அவதாரம்?

units.claim_summary: Mimamsa thinkers are credited with helping oppose Buddhism on Vedic authority and ritual grounds, even though Advaita later disputes important Mimamsa conclusions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பௌத்த கண்டனத்தில் மீமாம்ஸகர்களின் உதவி?

units.claim_summary: The critique of Buddhism is presented as operating on three fronts, combining ritual-scriptural, logical, and Vedantic objections rather than relying on a single line of attack.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பௌத்தத்தின் மும்முனை ஆக்ஷேபணை?

units.claim_summary: The chapter portrays the re-establishment of belief in Ishvara as part of the broader response to non-theistic or differently theistic schools during Shankara's attributed mission.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கடவுட் கொள்கையை நிலைநாட்டியது?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's apparent partiality toward particular practices or doctrines is explained as pedagogical adaptation to differing qualifications rather than as inconsistent attachment to factions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசார்யாளின் பாகுபாடு?

units.claim_summary: The appearance of teachers associated with the karma path is explained as necessary preparation for a mission that could restore Vedic action before leading qualified seekers toward knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கர்ம மார்க்கக்காரர்களின் அவதாரத்திற்குக் காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Traditions identifying Indra and Saraswati with supporting figures in Shankara's mission are used to portray the work as divinely assisted while emphasizing that the teacher's campaign is not dependent on royal power.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இந்திரன், ஸரஸ்வதி அவதாரங்கள் : அரசு ஸஹாயமின்றியே ஆசார்யாள் பணி?

units.claim_summary: Accounts of Kerala's religious and social past are surveyed as background for Shankara's birthplace, with historical claims kept as source-dependent traditions requiring external verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கேரள சரிதம்?

units.claim_summary: The discourse discusses Brahmin communities in early Tamil regions and the historical presence of Tamil in Kerala, preserving linguistic and migration claims as historiographical propositions rather than settled fact.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆதித் தமிழகத்தின் அந்தணர்கள் ; கேரளத்தில் தமிழ்?

units.claim_summary: Possible Kumbakonam connections are examined alongside the later history of the Kanchi Math's residence there, and conjecture about origins is kept distinct from documented institutional movement.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கும்பகோணப் பூர்வீகம்? காஞ்சி ஸ்ரீமடமும் கும்பகோணமும்?

units.claim_summary: The names Aryamba and Aryan are connected devotionally with Kanchi Kamakshi and Ayyappa, using linguistic and sacred associations rather than claiming that the names alone prove historical linkage.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆர்யாம்பா : காஞ்சி காமாக்ஷி ; ஆர்யன் : ஐயப்பன்?

units.claim_summary: The chosen land of an avatara is said to require religious fitness, and Kerala is presented within the tradition as possessing conditions suitable for Shankara's birth.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதார பூமிக்கான யோக்யதாம்சம்?

units.claim_summary: Shankara's parents are portrayed as pious householders whose discipline and devotion make them worthy participants in the hagiographic birth narrative.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பெற்றோரான புண்யசாலிகள்?

units.claim_summary: The parents' prayer at a sacred site near Thrissur is narrated as the setting for their request for a child, with the site's sanctity forming part of the hagiographic explanation of the birth.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருச்சூரில் வேண்டுதல்; க்ஷேத்ரச் சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: The boon narrative says the parents are offered a spiritually extraordinary but short-lived son rather than a merely long-lived ordinary child, presenting Shankara's birth as a divine response to prayer.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வரப் பிரதானம்?

units.claim_summary: Traditional features of Shankara Jayanti are related to the birth narrative and calendar, with ritual observance distinguished from historical proof of the exact date.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜயந்திச் சிறப்புக்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The discourse encourages public celebration of Shankara Jayanti as a means of remembering the acharya's teaching and renewing commitment to the religious ideals associated with him.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விமரிசையைக விழாக் கொண்டாடுக?

units.claim_summary: Kanchi is presented as having a special traditional connection with Shankara and his mission, a claim treated as institutional and hagiographic tradition rather than independently established chronology.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காஞ்சி மண்டலத்தின் விசேஷத் தொடர்பு?

units.claim_summary: Celebration of Shankara Jayanti at the Kamakshi temple is presented as an expression of Kanchi's traditional association with the acharya and the Goddess.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காமாக்ஷி ஆலயத்தில் சங்கர ஜயந்தி?

units.claim_summary: Outer offerings are subordinated to offering the mind itself, and silent contemplation is presented as a deeper form of worship in which thought is steadily turned toward the teacher and truth taught.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனத்தின் அர்ப்பணமும் மௌன மனனமும்?

units.claim_summary: The name given to Shankara is interpreted for its auspicious and theological significance, linking naming tradition to Shiva and to the mission later attributed to the child.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நாமகரணச் சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Katapayadi-style numerical interpretation is used to read a traditional verse as encoding the date of Shankara's siddhi; this is preserved as a traditional chronological argument rather than unquestioned history.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கடபயாதியில் ஸித்தி நாள்?

units.claim_summary: The traditional birth day is explained through lunar month, tithi, and other calendrical features that later observance uses to mark Shankara Jayanti.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதார நன்னாள்?

units.claim_summary: The meaning of 'Shankara' as one who brings auspiciousness is related to the acharya's mission, and later experience is offered devotionally as confirmation of that name rather than scientific evidence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘சம்’மைச் செய்வது; பிரத்யக்ஷச் சான்று?

units.claim_summary: The association of spring and the Vaisakha month with Shankara's birth is interpreted symbolically as fitting a teacher presented as renewing spiritual life.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வஸந்தகால வைசாக மாதப் பொருத்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Srisailam and other 'Arjuna' sacred sites are compared through names, mythology, and pilgrimage traditions, with the geographical and legendary strands kept distinct.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசைலம்; “அர்ஜுன” க்ஷேத்ரங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Traditional verses about Shankara's birth and siddhi are read as supporting a date in the sixth to fifth centuries BCE, an attributed chronological position requiring external historical verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – அவதார தின, ஸித்தி தின ச்லோகங்களில் கி.மு. 6-5 நூற்றாண்டுகள்?

units.claim_summary: The commonly cited modern chronology of 788–820 CE is presented as a competing view rather than silently replacing the earlier traditional dating.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – மாற்றுக் கருத்து (கி.பி. 788-820)?

units.claim_summary: A chronological argument using Kumarila and a quotation attributed to Kalidasa is examined, including its dependence on identifying texts and authors whose dates are themselves disputed.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – குமாரிலர் காட்டும் காளிதாஸனின் மேற்கோள் (மனஸ்ஸாக்ஷி ப்ரமாணம்)?

units.claim_summary: References to Buddhist doctrines in Shankara's commentaries are considered as chronological evidence, but the argument is limited by uncertainty about when particular Buddhist positions and authors flourished.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – ஆசார்ய பாஷ்யத்தில் பௌத்தக் கொள்கைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Later-era references found in works attributed to Shankara are examined as dating evidence while allowing the possibility of later authorship, interpolation, or attribution to a different Shankara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – ஆசார்ய ஸ்தோத்ரங்களில் கி.பி. குறிப்புக்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The reference to Purnavarman is considered for chronology, but uncertainty over the ruler's identity prevents treating the passage as a decisive date marker.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – பூர்ணவர்மனைப் பற்றிய குறிப்பு?

units.claim_summary: The discourse criticizes dismissive Western treatments of traditional chronology and argues that research assumptions may carry cultural bias; this is represented as the author's historiographical polemic, not a neutral finding.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – மேல்நாட்டவரின் பரிஹாஸமும் உள்நோக்கமும்?

units.claim_summary: Indian calendrical systems and Kali-yuga reckoning are invoked to explain how traditional dates are preserved, while conversion to modern chronology is acknowledged as a source of dispute.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – கலியுகத்தில் நமது காலக் கணக்குகள்?

units.claim_summary: Traditional historical and hagiographic works are listed as evidence for Shankara's life, with their differing dates and narrative purposes requiring source-critical comparison rather than simple harmonization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – நமது சரித்ர ஆதார நூல்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The identification of Megasthenes' Sandrokottos is treated as a central chronological question, and alternative identifications are explored for their consequences to the dating of Indian dynasties and Shankara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – மையக் கேள்வி : மெகஸ்தனிஸ் சொல்லும் ‘ ஸன்ட்ர கோட்டஸ் ‘ யார் ??

units.claim_summary: The date of Kalidasa is examined because it affects linked arguments about Kumarila and Shankara; competing chronologies are preserved rather than collapsed.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – காளிதாஸன் விஷய ம்?

units.claim_summary: References to Buddhist authors conventionally dated in the Common Era are tested against the proposed earlier Shankara chronology, with dependence on the dating of those authors made explicit.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – கிறிஸ்து சகாப்த பௌத்த நூலாசிரியர்கள் விஷயம்?

units.claim_summary: Earlier Buddhas and Jinas are distinguished from the historically familiar founders or later teachers so that textual references to those names are not automatically used as late chronological anchors.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – பூர்வகால புத்தர்களும், ஜினர்களும்?

units.claim_summary: The rise of Mahayana is considered as a dating issue, but the brief discussion treats the label's chronology as contested rather than decisive evidence by itself.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – மஹாயான விஷயம்?

units.claim_summary: The 'Dravida child' expression is examined as possible historical evidence, while alternative identifications and literary meanings prevent a confident chronological inference.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – “த்ரவிட சிசு” விஷயம்?

units.claim_summary: The phrase interpreted as 'enemy of the son' is examined for possible identification with a historical figure, but the discourse keeps the inference tentative because the wording admits more than one reading.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்ரீசங்கரரின் கால நிர்ணயம் – “ஸுத த்ரோஹி” விஷயம்?
